title: Android JS bridges (SevenFriendsAndroid, SfInsets) reachable from third-party iframes in chat link previews
description: MainActivity registers NativeNotices and Insets_ with addJavascriptInterface; Android injects them into every frame. The chat page frames any framable https page (server stores final URL as embedUrl) with sandbox allow-scripts allow-same-origin after the recipient taps 'Show preview'. No bridge method checks the calling origin.
root_cause: addJavascriptInterface bridges have no per-origin guard while chat frames arbitrary third-party pages.
intended_behavior: Only the first-party origin (sevenfriends.io) may call the native bridge.

trace.description: addJavascriptInterface(NativeNotices, 'SevenFriendsAndroid'), no origin restriction (line 71: SfInsets).
framingAllowed/pageAllowsFrame accept any public framable https page; linkOf stores final URL as embedUrl.
iframe [src]=frameUrl(embedUrl) with sandbox allow-scripts allow-same-origin after 'Show preview'.
deviceName(), deviceModel(), status(), share(), openNotificationSettings(), sync() act without origin check.

evidence.description: server.url is https://sevenfriends.io so the iframe is a distinct third-party origin.

conditions: Attacker page is public https text/html 2xx without X-Frame-Options / restrictive frame-ancestors
Subframe injection of JavascriptInterface objects is standard WebView behaviour but was not executed here
execution: NOT EXECUTED (no OS sandbox). Planned: emulator with dummy accounts; host page logging typeof window.SevenFriendsAndroid and deviceName(); send URL in chat; tap Show preview.
impact: Disclosure of device name/model and notification state to a third-party site; phishing-style share chooser and nuisance UI; cosmetic notification-channel changes. No credentials, tokens or files; sound URIs cannot be attacker-controlled.
confidence: medium-high (source complete; runtime behaviour documented but not executed)
remediation: Replace addJavascriptInterface with WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener / addDocumentStartJavaScript using allowedOriginRules ['https://sevenfriends.io']; and/or restrict embedUrl to allowlisted player hosts and enforce frame-src.
regression_test: Instrumented Android test: in a cross-origin iframe, window.SevenFriendsAndroid and window.SfInsets are undefined; on https://sevenfriends.io they are defined.

title: Account erase deletes other users' pending invitations that match the eraser's unverified typed phone or email
description: eraseUser probes all users' friends entries (collection group) by the eraser's emailLower/email/phoneKey/phone/verifiedPhone with no verification check and deletes unlinked matches plus the inviter-side request, signal and safebox for that connection.
root_cause: Unverified identifiers (token.email regardless of email_verified; typed profile phone, last 8 digits) are treated as proof of ownership in erase.
intended_behavior: Erase removes entries other people wrote for this person, sound only for identifiers the eraser has proven.

trace.description: Typed phone stored as phone/phoneKey with no proof (users.ts:30 likewise stores emailLower from an unverified token email).
DELETE /users/me with confirm DELETE calls eraseUser.
Probes built without verified check; global collectionGroup('friends') query; only entries linked to another uid are skipped (line 123).
Matched pending entries, requests, signals and safebox for the connection are deleted.

evidence.description: verifiedIdentity documents the intended gate but erase does not use it.

conditions: Attacker's profile phone (or unverified token email) equals the victim's identifier
An inviter has a pending unlinked entry for the victim
Email variant needs Firebase Auth to allow unverified email sign-up (console fact, not visible)
execution: NOT EXECUTED. Planned: emulator test with two dummy users (see regression_test).
likelihood: medium for phone path; email path depends on Auth console
impact: Pending invitations (and attached request/signal/safebox of unconfirmed connections) of other users are deleted; recoverable by re-adding. Confirmed or other-linked connections untouched; attacker's account is destroyed (one-shot).
remediation: Probe by emailLower only when account.emailVerified === true and by phone only when verifiedPhone is set; drop typed account.phone/email probes; keep linkedUid==uid probe.
regression_test: A has unverified typed phone equal to V's; B has pending unlinked entry for V; after eraseUser(A) B's entry remains. Case with verifiedPhone still deletes. Same pair for email.

title: Friend-request sender's display name rendered through [innerHTML] without escaping
description: Translation strings '{{ fromName }}' are bound with [innerHTML] in notifications.html and pending.html; the i18n layer does not escape params and the backend only trims/slices names to 100 chars.
root_cause: Untrusted name interpolated into an HTML string that is bound as innerHTML (friend-join.html uses esc(); these sites were missed).
intended_behavior: The name displays as plain text inside bold markup.

trace.description: text(value,max) only trims and slices; used for profile and circle-profile names.
listPendingRequests returns fromName raw.
[innerHTML]=t('notifications.strongFromnameStrong', {fromName}).
Same pattern.

evidence.description: CSP is Report-Only so remote img/links are not blocked.

conditions: Attacker can set a display name and send a friend request
Angular sanitizer keeps a/img with https URLs (known behaviour; not executed here)
execution: NOT EXECUTED. Planned: render Pending with fromName containing an anchor and img; inspect DOM.
impact: Link/phishing text and a remote tracking image inside a trusted card. No script execution (sanitizer strips script, on* handlers, javascript: URLs). Same class at friend-recovery.html:35 (confirmed friends only).
remediation: Render the name with text interpolation in a template <strong> element, or HTML-escape fromName (existing esc()) before t(); apply to friend-recovery.html:35 too; enforce CSP.
regression_test: Component tests for notifications/pending with fromName 'x' assert no img/a rendered and literal text shown.

title: Pending invitations can be claimed via an unverified email or a typed phone number; the unverified warning can be suppressed
description: syncIncomingInvites matches other users' pending entries by token.email (no email_verified check) and by the user-typed profile phoneKey. First claimant is linked and the real invitee is skipped afterwards. unverifiedDetails returns [] whenever the claimant has any verified detail, so a typed phone claimed on an account with a verified email shows no warning.
root_cause: Invite matching uses unverified/typed identifiers instead of verifiedIdentity(); mitigation (warning) fails for the typed-phone case.
intended_behavior: Reachability without verification is a documented, warned trade-off (invites.ts header, docs/guide/connections.md); validation.ts says only verified identities should be used to find people.

trace.description: Typed phone stored as phoneKey without proof.
Probes: token.email (unverified) and account.phoneKey.
First claimer wins; entries linked to another uid are skipped.
Creates request for claimant; line 75 sets linkedUid=claimant.
unverifiedDetails returns [] if any detail is verified.

evidence.description: verifiedIdentity intent not applied by invites.ts.

conditions: Inviter added a pending entry by email/phone for someone not yet linked
Attacker signed in, visibility not private, runs the check before the real invitee
Inviter manually accepts; inviter sees the attacker's own account name
execution: NOT EXECUTED. Planned: emulator test (see regression_test).
impact: Attacker can become a confirmed friend in the invitee's place (one seat) and block the invitation; limited by manual accept and a visible differing name.
remediation: Probe by email only when token.email_verified===true and by phone only from SMS-verified token.phone_number (verifiedIdentity()); drop account.phoneKey from probes; or make unverifiedDetails flag a typed phone.
regression_test: verification.test.ts: B (verified email, typed A's phone) runs /notifications/check; assert no request for B and no linkedUid set; unverified-email token does not claim an email invite.

title: Windows wrapper treats every *.firebaseapp.com host as in-app
description: IsInside matches host == h or EndsWith('.'+h) for the bare multi-tenant domain firebaseapp.com, so chat links to attacker-registered Firebase Hosting sites open inside the app (NewWindowRequested/NavigationStarting return without handing off to the system browser).
root_cause: Suffix wildcard allow-list entry for a shared hosting domain; only sevenfriends.firebaseapp.com (auth handler) is needed.
intended_behavior: Only the app's own pages and sign-in popup stay inside; all other links open in the system browser.

trace.description: Non-own chat URL renders as <a target=_blank>, raising NewWindowRequested.
Inside list contains 'firebaseapp.com'.
IsInside uses EndsWith('.'+h).
Returns early (no hand-off) when IsInside; NavigationStarting line 185 likewise.

evidence.description: Permissions gated by exact host on first three Inside entries; no host-object/WebMessage bridge exists.

conditions: Victim clicks an https://*.firebaseapp.com link in chat
Popup chrome (address bar absence) not verified from source
execution: NOT EXECUTED. Planned: run Windows app with dummy account and a self-owned test firebaseapp.com page.
impact: In-app phishing/spoofing window; no mic/camera/clipboard permission, no native bridge, no access to app storage (different origin).
remediation: Replace 'firebaseapp.com' with the exact auth host 'sevenfriends.firebaseapp.com'; exact-match the auth host.
regression_test: IsInside: sevenfriends.io, sevenfriends.firebaseapp.com, accounts.google.com true; attacker.firebaseapp.com, evilfirebaseapp.com, http://sevenfriends.io false.

title: Account-existence lookup limited only by per-instance, per-uid in-memory counters
description: POST /friends/lookup and POST /friends (onlyIfOnApp) return found/none for an email or phone (private accounts excluded; unverified emailLower/phoneKey match). tooManySearches (30/h) and tooManyAdds (100/h) are module-level Maps keyed by uid, per instance (maxInstances 10).
claimed_root_cause: Rate limit keyed on a free-to-mint principal and held per instance.

trace.description: POST /lookup applies tooManySearches(uid).
In-memory Map, 30 per hour per instance.
findAccounts returns existence by emailLower/phoneKey.

blockers: Whether Firebase Auth sign-up is open/throttled and whether App Check or other abuse controls are enforced (console facts, not in source)
Existence is the documented purpose of the lookup; only the strength of the limit is in question

local: Call lookup 31 times with one uid, expect 429; repeat with a fresh uid.
deployment: Owner checks Auth sign-up throttling and App Check enforcement in the Firebase console.

claimed_root_cause: own() guard tests link.url, not the redirect-resolved embedUrl, so a redirect to sevenfriends.io frames the app itself with allow-scripts allow-same-origin.

trace.description: own(message.link.url) checked, embedUrl framed at line 166.

evidence.description: Redirects followed without rejecting the app origin.

reason: Mechanics are real but no security effect: attacker runs no script in the app origin and cannot reach window.parent; frame shows the victim their own app and only the route/query is attacker-chosen. Kept as hardening (test own(embedUrl); reject app-origin final URLs; enforce frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options).

claimed_root_cause: POST /keys/list restart:true is authorised only by a signature from a key the same login just published; startOver then deletes other keys and rescue backups.

trace.description: restart skips the previous-signer check.
startOver/removeTraces delete keys, backups, push devices.

evidence.description: Documents that the server cannot tell which device calls and a stolen login can retire any key; device-signed requests are named future work.

reason: Behaviour is the documented lost-all-devices path and an accepted 'not done on purpose' gap; key deletion is fixed rule 10; history stays closed (rules 6, 12); friends with a pin are blocked by a warning. Rejected as a new defect. Residual note for the owner: restart sends no push to old devices and has no cooling-off; the documented fix is a request signed by an existing device key.

claimed_root_cause: Friend recovery (Way 2) wraps for every server-listed key of the requester instead of only the signed-list keys.

trace.description: activeOf uses publishedKeysOf.

evidence.description: Fixed rule 5 requires every key in use for Way 2; rule 9: friend approval is the human check; recovery-by-friend.md already names this scenario.

reason: Exactly what the fixed owner rules require; rules not challenged. Any stronger check (e.g. one-time code step 7 in recovery-by-friend.md) is an owner design decision, not a code violation.

claimed_root_cause: Accounts with keys but no signed list trust every published key for new messages.

trace.description: recipientKeysOf returns all keys with no list head.

evidence.description: 'Existing users': legacy accounts keep an older lock with no list/migration until they rotate.

reason: Documented accepted legacy behaviour; the added key is a waiting key that gets no history and prompts the owner (rule 6). Optional hardening: exclude waiting keys from recipientKeysOf/limit for accounts without a list.
